subject: Request: SLA carve for customer-controlled VPC (shared responsibility)
messages:
From: Gina Morales <gina@stratoscale.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA request: private VPC deployment (Stratoscale)

Hi Karthik / Redwood team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we move toward a Private VPC deployment for our production workload, procurement has asked us to capture the availability and latency commitments that will apply when the control plane is managed by Redwood but the inference nodes live in our AWS VPC.

Two asks from our side:
- Explicit carveout language that makes it clear that infrastructure/network incidents originating in our VPC (or our cloud provider) are not counted against the Redwood uptime SLA.
- An agreed maximum p99 tail latency target for requests routed through the customer VPC (we propose p99 < 350ms for 1k token requests) unless constrained by our egress NAT/transit.

I've attached the procurement form with our preferred language and highlighted places where we expect a shared-responsibility callout. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept those carveouts and/or propose alternative wording?

Best,
Gina Morales\Director, Cloud Ops\Stratoscale

Attachment: Stratoscale_SLA_Exception_Request.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Gina Morales <gina@stratoscale.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: private VPC deployment (Stratoscale)

Hi Gina —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attached form. We're excited to get Stratoscale onto Private VPC. High level: we can accept a shared-responsibility carveout for customer-controlled network and hardware incidents, but we need to be explicit about the operational signals and monitoring windows that define those carveouts so there is no ambiguity at incident time.

Quick proposals:
- Carveout applies when the root cause is isolated to customer-controlled infrastructure (VPC networking, customer-managed bastion/NAT, or customer-managed instance lifecycle). Such incidents will be excluded from Redwood uptime calculations provided Stratoscale: (a) shares cloud provider incident IDs or VPC flow logs within 24 hours, and (b) opens a support ticket with relevant logs within the same window.
- For latency SLOs in customer VPC mode, we can commit to p95 < 200ms and p99 < 400ms for inference requests under typical token distributions, with the caveat that third-party transit (customer NAT/proxy) can add variability. We can provide a latency profile report from our test harness run in your VPC as part of the onboarding to set baseline expectations.

I've attached an initial draft of suggested wording. Looping in Dev (SE) for technical verification and Lauren to coordinate legal/contract language.

Next steps: Dev — can you run the quick latency baseline in Stratoscale's VPC sandbox this week? Lauren/Evelyn — please advise on whether the proposed evidence windows (24h logs + provider incident ID) are acceptable to legal.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlined-sla-draft.docx

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, gina@stratoscale.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: private VPC deployment (Stratoscale)

Karthik / Gina —

I ran a short baseline using the sandbox VPC creds you shared (thanks, Gina). High level observations:
- Under controlled conditions (no extra NAT/proxy hops) our p95 for 1k-token inference is ~120ms and p99 ~260ms when the worker is in the same AZ.
- When requests transit through a managed proxy (added jitter + ~40–80ms tail), p99 can hit ~380–450ms depending on burst and TCP windowing.
- If Stratoscale plans to use central egress (single NAT gateway) across AZs, that will add more variability; we recommend a multi-AZ egress or per-AZ ENIs for predictable latency.

I'll include the raw run logs in the Drive link. Based on this, the proposed p99 < 400ms is achievable with recommended egress topology and a 99th percentile-focused routing policy from Redwood. We should make the SLA conditional on network topology and on Stratoscale providing flow logs when requesting an SLA exclusion.

—Dev
Dev Patel\Solutions Engineer\Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request: private VPC deployment (Stratoscale)

Thanks for the context. Legal's suggested redlines (high level):
1) Shared Responsibility: carveouts acceptable when customer demonstrates provider-side incident or VPC-level evidence. We prefer to define the acceptable evidence as: cloud provider incident ID OR VPC flow logs demonstrating packet drops/route blackholing AND timing correlation with Redwood monitoring.
2) Evidence window: we can accept customer-supplied evidence within 72 hours rather than 24 to allow for time zone/ops shift differences, but require a ticket to be opened within 24 hours to preserve triage workflows.
3) Latency commitments: rather than hard number in the master SLA for customer VPC, we'll add an appendix to the contract that records the onboarding latency baseline (test harness report) and makes the p99 target an onboarding-defined value. This avoids a one-size-fits-all promise.

Evelyn recommends the following contract language snippet: "For Private/VPC deployments, the Service Level Commitment shall exclude incidents where Customer-controlled infrastructure (including but not limited to VPC networking, customer-managed NAT, or customer-hosted proxies) is the root cause, provided Customer supplies timely evidence as set forth in Appendix A. Latency objectives for Customer VPC mode will be captured in an onboarding appendix and may be adjusted by mutual written agreement."

If the customer pushes back on 72h, we can accept 48h as a compromise.

-Lauren (on behalf of Legal/Evelyn)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Gina Morales <gina@stratoscale.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, procurement@stratoscale.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Proposed SLA carve and onboarding appendix (Stratoscale)

Gina / Ben / Procurement —

Thanks for working through this with us. Summarizing the agreed approach so we can close the procurement thread:
- Shared-responsibility carveout: Redwood will exclude incidents attributable to customer-controlled infrastructure from uptime calculations, contingent on Customer submitting either (a) the cloud provider incident reference, or (b) VPC flow logs demonstrating network-level failure, and opening a Redwood support ticket within 24 hours. We are willing to accept evidence up to 72 hours, but ticket opening within 24 hours is required.
- Latency: Rather than a fixed top-line p99 in the master SLA, we will capture an onboarding latency appendix that records the baseline test-harness results run in Stratoscale's VPC. Based on Dev's run, an initial baseline p99 of ~260–380ms is reasonable; final p99 objective will be set in the appendix after you complete the multi-AZ egress configuration we recommended.
- Evidence & operational process: Redwood will provide a template Appendix A that lists required log formats and timestamps; Redwood will also share a latency-report PDF from our baseline run (Drive link).

Next steps:
1) Gina — please confirm you are comfortable with the 24h ticket-opening requirement and whether Stratoscale wants us to accept 48h instead of 72h for submitted evidence.
2) Once confirmed, Evelyn will prepare the appendix language (short redline) and route for signature; we will send a DocuSign link.
3) Dev will schedule one more baseline run after your egress change — we recommend that before you push to prod.

I'll attach the redlined SLA and the DocuSign link in a follow-up email.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting you live.

Best,
Karthik Iyer\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference
